newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso pares strength at close on dlr cover.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso pares strength at close on dlr cover.

text.p: The Mexican peso moderated earlier gains towards the close as local banks took advantage of peso strength to cover short dollar positions, traders said.

"The peso came under pressure in late trade due to (dollar) shorts some local banks had to cover. I still feel the peso is strong, however, as dollars were in supply for most of the day," a trader said.
The benchmark 48-hour peso and the 24-hour contract closed 0.6 and 0.9 centavos firmer, respectively, at 7.8240/7.8280 and 7.8180/7.8230 per dollar.
The 48-hour peso had firmed up to 7.8080/7.8170 per dollar in mid-morning trade.

"Although volume was not heavy, you could tell foreign dealers were selling dollars. Some were dumping long positions, as it was expensive to hold on to them, and others were buying pesos ahead of (Tuesday's) primary auction," a money market analyst said.

Traders said the peso's performance on Tuesday would depend to a large degree on whether the bourse recovered from its slump on Monday, and on market forecasts for the primary auction of government securities.
Same-day peso contracts earlier closed 4.8 centavos firmer at 7.7990/7.8040 per dollar.
